question.problem:
Consider the equivalence relation $∼$ on $Z,$ defined by $x∼y$ if $7\,|\,(x-y).$ Which of the following equivalence classes contain the element $2?$

I. $[1]$

II. $[0]$

III. $[9]$
question.worked_solution:
We have $2\in [x]$ if $2∼x.$ Using the definition of the given equivalence relation, we require

$$
\begin{aligned}7\,|\,(2-x).\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now consider each of the given equivalence classes.

- $2\notin [1]$ because $7∤(2-1)\,\times $

- $2\notin [0]$ because $7∤(2-0)\,\times $

- $2\in [9]$ because $7\,|\,(2-9)\,✓$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
